transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hello, doctor. Well, I'm here because... I keep hearing these very clear voices. It happens in my apartment mostly, and sometimes when I'm in empty museum rooms. It sounds just like women whispering from behind the walls, and they keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. It's very distinct, so I thought I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
When you hear these voices, do they seem to be coming from outside your body, like they're actually in the room with you, or do they feel like they're inside your head?

They definitely sound like they are coming from outside of me. Like I mentioned a moment ago, it sounds exactly like they are behind the physical walls of my apartment. It's not just a thought in my head... it's actual women whispering. When I'm in those empty museum rooms, it's the exact same thing. The voices are out there in the room with me, just on the other side of the plaster, telling me about the photographs.

Over the past few months or weeks when you've been hearing these voices, have you also experienced periods where your mood was significantly elevated or depressed, or have the voices been occurring mostly when your mood has been relatively normal?

Well, let me think about that... yes, they happen even when my mood is completely normal. For example, there was a period of several weeks recently where I wasn't feeling especially energized or... or grand, I guess you could say. My mood was just level. 

But even then, I still heard the whispers in the apartment. And during that whole time, I remained convinced that the arts people were monitoring my phone. So, it definitely still happens when my mood is just regular, not just when it's up or down.

When did you first start hearing these voices and believing that the arts people were monitoring your phone? Did this all begin during a time when your mood was normal, or did it start during a period when you were feeling unusually energized, depressed, or otherwise different from your baseline?

Let me think back... The voices and the certainty that people are watching my archive, they've been present for about eight months now. 

And when it all first started back then, my mood was just normal. I wasn't feeling unusually energized or down or anything like that. Everything was pretty much at my regular baseline when the whispering and the monitoring began.

During these past 8 months, have you ever had a period where you needed significantly less sleep than usual but still felt rested and energetic, or where your thoughts seemed to be racing much faster than normal?

Yes, I have. There have been stretches where... well, I really only need to sleep about two or three hours a night. And I'll wake up way before dawn feeling completely ready for the day. I don't feel tired at all. I just tell myself that sleep is for people who do not have an archive to rescue. So I just get up and get right to work.

When you first started hearing the voices and believing people were monitoring your archive 8 months ago, had you already been experiencing those periods of needing only 2-3 hours of sleep and feeling very energetic? Or did the reduced sleep need and high energy start sometime after the voices and monitoring beliefs began?

The voices definitely started first. Like I mentioned, my mood was just normal when the whispering and the monitoring began eight months ago. The sleep changes came a bit later. 

But once that started... well, if I look back at the whole eight months, those bursts of getting very little sleep, having all these racing plans, spending money, and just having this furious energy... they have taken up about six of those months in total.

When those periods of needing only 2-3 hours of sleep and having all that racing energy and furious activity started a few months into those 8 months - did the voices and the belief about people monitoring your archive continue exactly as they had been, or did they become more intense or more elaborate at that time?

Yes, they kept going right through it. During those times when I was only sleeping a couple of hours and just racing from one archive task to the next... I was still hearing the women whispering. And I was still absolutely certain that the museum board was tracking everything I was doing. The voices and the monitoring didn't stop just because I had all that energy.

During those periods when you were sleeping only 2-3 hours and had all that racing energy and furious activity - were there any times when the voices from behind the walls actually went away or became much quieter, even for a few days or a week?

No, they didn't go away or even get quiet. Like I was just saying, even during the times when I was sleeping just a few hours and racing around from one archive task to another... I was still hearing the women’s voices the entire time. And I was still completely certain that the museum board was tracking my work. It never stopped, not even for a day.

The hallucinations are experienced as external (outside the body, in the room) and remain stable even during periods of elevated mood and reduced sleep.
